1.title: Containers: Registry, Instances and Container Apps
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Containers: Registry, Instances and Container Apps. It covers the exam area Deploy and manage Azure compute resources. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Create and manage an Azure container registry. Provision a container by using Azure Container Instances. Provision a container by using Azure Container Apps. Manage sizing and scaling for containers. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (twenty-twenty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: Containers in one page
1.text: Containers in one page. A container packages an application and its dependencies so it runs the same everywhere. It shares the host O S kernel, so it starts fast and is lighter than a V M. A container image is the template; a container registry stores images.

1.title: Containers in one page, continued
1.text: Containers in one page. The figure shows this: Choosing between Azure Container Registry, Container Instances and Container Apps.

1.title: Azure Container Registry (ACR)
1.text: Azure Container Registry (A C R). Azure Container Registry is a private registry for container images (Docker format) and artifacts. S K Us. Basic, Standard, Premium; Premium adds geo-replication, private endpoints and content trust. Push and pull. docker login name dot azurecr dot io, then docker push and docker pull. Authentication. Microsoft Entra identity (recommended), service principal, managed identity, or the admin account (for testing). A C R Tasks. Build images in Azure (on commit, on base image update, on a schedule). Roles. Acr Pull, Acr Push for access. Exam tip: "Replicate the registry to several regions" equals A C R Premium with geo-replication. Avoid the admin account in production.

1.title: Azure Container Instances (ACI)
1.text: Azure Container Instances (A C I). A C I runs containers directly on Azure with no V M or orchestrator to manage. It is the fastest and simplest way, billed per second. Container group. Several containers sharing a lifecycle, network and storage on one host (like a pod). Size. C P U and memory are set when you create the group; to change, recreate it. Networking. Public I P and D N S name label, or V net deployment (private). Restart policy. Always, On Failure, Never (use Never or On Failure for batch jobs). Storage. Mount Azure Files shares for persistent data. Use for: simple apps, batch jobs, build agents, bursts. Not for: long-running microservices needing autoscale and ingress (use Container Apps).

1.title: Azure Container Apps
1.text: Azure Container Apps. Azure Container Apps is a serverless platform for microservices and containerized apps (built on Kubernetes with no cluster management). Environment. A secure boundary (V net, logging) that hosts several container apps. Revisions. Immutable versions; traffic splitting for blue or green or canary. Ingress. H T T P or H T T P S external or internal endpoint. Autoscale. K E D A rules (H T T P requests, queue length, C P U, memory, custom) and scale to zero. Replicas. Set minimum and maximum; each replica gets the C P U and memory you assign. Exam tip: "Run a containerized microservice that scales on queue length and can scale to zero, without managing Kubernetes" equals Azure Container Apps. "Run one container quickly with no scaling logic" equals A C I.

1.title: Sizing and scaling
1.text: Sizing and scaling. A C I. Sizing: C P U and memory per container at creation. Scaling: No built-in autoscale; create more groups. Container Apps. Sizing: C P U and memory per replica. Scaling: Min or max replicas and scale rules. Exam tip: Container Apps equals serverless microservices with scale rules; A C I equals a quick container group; A C R equals the image store.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company wants to store private container images and replicate them across regions. Which service and skew fit? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Azure Container Registry Premium. Geo-replication is a Premium feature of A C R.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team wants to run a short batch container without managing servers and pay per second. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Azure Container Instances. A C I runs containers on demand with per-second billing.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A microservice should scale from zero based on queue length. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Azure Container Apps. Container Apps supports K E D A rules and scale to zero.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. How can C P U and memory of a container group in A C I be changed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Recreate the container group with new values. A C I resources are set at creation.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which A C I restart policy fits a batch job that should not restart after success? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: On Failure or Never. Batch jobs use On Failure or Never.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which Container Apps feature allows traffic to be split between versions? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Revisions. Revisions are immutable versions with traffic splitting.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does A C R store? Answer: Container images and artifacts. Question two. What is a container group in A C I? Answer: Containers sharing a lifecycle, network and storage on one host. Question three. What engine does Container Apps use for scale rules? Answer: K E D A.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Can Container Apps scale to zero? Answer: Yes. Question five. Which A C R skew supports geo-replication? Answer: Premium. Question six. How is A C I billed? Answer: Per second of C P U and memory used.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. A C R: Basic or Standard or Premium; Premium geo-replication; A C R Tasks; Entra auth. A C I: quickest, no orchestrator, container groups, fixed size, per-second billing. Container Apps: serverless microservices, revisions, ingress, K E D A autoscale, scale to zero.
